notes: File sizes are read from the Hugging Face model API (?blobs=true) on the retrieval date, without downloading.

JevBench ranks and scores come from JevBench v1.4.2 (results JSON sha256 ac14e206dde5..., generated 2026-09-24), published at https://benchmarkheaven.com/jev-models and https://benchmarkheaven.com/api/jevbench/v1.4.2.

'measured' latency figures are from local runs on rented GPUs on 25 Sep 2026 over 50 public JevBench items (a sanity check, not an official re-score). Everything else about speed is an assumption and says so.
Memory thresholds (min_*_gb) are assumptions: file size plus a runtime/context margin. They are not measured on every device.
Bonsai 2's capability as a routed coding model is an assumption: the vendor's model card reports its benchmarks; this repository has not measured it.

bonsai.runtime: Needs the PrismML llama.cpp fork (https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp): stock llama.cpp rejects PQ2_0/PTQ1_0 (vendor model card). Backends: CUDA, Metal, CPU.

jev_tiers.measured: RTX 4090 24 GB: 40 ms warm median decision, 43/50 public items (25 Sep 2026). Does not fit an 8 GB RTX 3070.
jev_tiers.note: Pin the benchmarked revision; the current HEAD is a later version. Opt-in only, because the router's local backend expects an OpenAI-compatible llama-server endpoint.

jev_tiers.measured: Not measured here. The model card reports 228/231 public answers identical to bf16.
jev_tiers.note: The benchmarked JevK5 version is v0.2; the card's newer v0.3 files are the author's own numbers, not a JevBench row.

jev_tiers.measured: RTX 3070 8 GB, llama.cpp CUDA: 189 ms warm median decision, 43/50 public items (25 Sep 2026). CPU latency not measured.
jev_tiers.note: Quantized: the card reports 219/231 public answers identical to bf16.

jev_tiers.serving: in-process: the router's existing `classifier: {backend: local}` (pip extra [local], CPU torch)
jev_tiers.measured: x86-64 Linux CPU: 2.9 GB peak RAM (README). RTX 3070 native ORT CUDA int4: 1.40 s median, 27/50.
jev_tiers.note: Much weaker than JevK5 on hard items; the fallback when nothing larger fits.

jev_tiers.note: Last fallback, for the web demo only. For the router itself use the heuristic classifier or hosted Jev (your own TYPESAFE_API_KEY).
